decisions.rationale: This is a full species mirror, so I pick the four that best win the speed and nuke races. Lead Mega Charizard Y + Garchomp: Drought sun turns Heat Wave/Weather Ball into spread nukes (their Whimsicott is 2x weak, Kingambit 2x weak behind only Occa) while Jolly Garchomp at 169 Speed outruns their Charizard/Floette and threatens 4x Rock Slide on their Charizard, denying their own Mega Zard. Back: Whimsicott for Prankster Tailwind/Encore control with Focus Sash insurance, and Kingambit as my Fairy resist (their Mega Floette Light of Ruin under Fairy Aura is their scariest attack) with Sucker Punch priority plus Low Kick, which their Kingambit set has no answer to (Occa Berry, no Low Kick). I keep Floettite home because I only get one Mega and Charizard-Mega-Y's sun is my engine; Fairy Aura would also amplify their three Fairy attackers.

SERIES vs mirror team (identical six species both sides). Opponent set differences from mine: their Charizard has AncientPower (Rock, hits my Zard) instead of SolarBeam; their Garchomp has Earthquake + PoisonJab + Roseli Berry (halves Fairy) instead of Stomping Tantrum/Life Orb; their Kingambit has Protect + Occa Berry (halves Fire, so Heat Wave won't OHKO it) and NO Low Kick; their Basculegion holds Life Orb (mine Mystic Water). My Kingambit's Chople Berry is dead weight - nothing on their team has a Fighting move; my Low Kick (Kingambit weighs 120kg = 100 BP) is my best mirror-breaker vs their Kingambit.
Key numbers/plans: my Garchomp 169 Spe can speed-tie their Jolly Garchomp (134-169) and outruns their Charizard (120-152), Floette (123-158). My Whimsicott 184 Spe is at/above their Whimsicott ceiling (149-184). Both sides carry two Mega Stones; I intend Charizard-Mega-Y (Drought) as default. Avoid megaing Floette: Fairy Aura buffs their Whimsicott/Floette Moonblast+LightofRuin too. Their Mega Floette (Fairy Aura, 155 SpA, LightofRuin) is their biggest nuke - answer with Kingambit (Steel resist) or Charizard pressure; their Garchomp's Roseli blunts my Fairy attacks. Sun helps their Charizard's HeatWave/WeatherBall equally, so watch for mirror sun trades. Bring plan G1: Charizard/Garchomp lead, Whimsicott + Kingambit back. If this loses, consider Basculegion (Adaptability WaveCrash/AquaJet) as a faster-priority answer or Floette for the LightofRuin nuke.

decisions.rationale: Mirror match: lead Whimsicott+Charizard for Prankster Tailwind + Mega-Y Drought. My Whimsicott at 184 Spe wins/ties the Prankster Speed bracket for first Tailwind. Charizard-Y under Tailwind (210 Spe) outspeeds everything and Ancient Power is a tech for the Charizard mirror (Rock is SE vs Fire/Flying). Back: Basculegion (Life Orb Adaptability Wave Crash is a nuke under Tailwind, Aqua Jet for priority cleanup) and Garchomp (Rock Slide spread flinches, Earthquake coverage, Roseli Berry to tank Fairy hits from Floette). Key edge: my Basculegion hits harder (LO vs Mystic Water) and my Kingambit has Protect (opponent's doesn't), but I save Kingambit for game 2/3 reads. Opponent's Solar Beam in sun threatens Garchomp/Basculegion so I keep them in back until sun is controlled or Charizard is dealt with.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp (169 Spe, faster than their Charizard) Rock Slide is a guaranteed OHKO on their Charizard even through Mega (4x, spread) and chips Whimsicott to its Focus Sash; Mega Charizard-Y's sun-boosted Heat Wave then finishes Whimsicott through the sash, removing their Prankster Tailwind/Encore support immediately. Megaing is safe here because their Charizard should be dead before it can abuse the sun, and Drought gives me the stronger long-game Fire pressure.

decisions.rationale: Bringing Garchomp is superior to Basculegion here. Under Tailwind, my Garchomp (314 Spe) outspeedes both opponents and can Rock Slide for 4x SE on opposing Charizard (70-160%, possible OHKO) while my Charizard follows up with Ancient Power (4x SE) to guarantee the KO. Even if my Charizard falls to the opposing Garchomp's Rock Slide (70-160% threat), my Garchomp outspeedes theirs (314 vs 134-169) and wins the mirror with Dragon Claw (2x SE). Basculegion is a poor bring: Wave Crash is only neutral vs Garchomp (25-55%, no KO), and opposing Charizard's Solar Beam threatens an OHKO (62-133%). Garchomp takes Solar Beam neutrally (Grass vs Dragon/Ground = 1x), making it far safer. Preserving Basculegion for later also keeps Life Orb Adaptability damage as a late-game wallbreaker option.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

I'm up 4-2, so preserve Mega Zard instead of trading it: under their Tailwind both foes move first, and Basculegion's LO Adaptability Wave Crash alone is 83-122% on my Zard (Rock Slide finishes anyway). decisions.rationale: Basculegion is the opponent's last Pokémon at 76%; Garchomp Dragon Claw (40-76%) plus Kingambit Kowtow Cleave (74-141%) is a guaranteed KO if both connect, and Kowtow alone (min 74%) kills once Life Orb chip lands, so even if Basculegion KOs Garchomp first I still win this turn. Sucker Punch was rejected because Aqua Jet's priority plus Tailwind speed would make it fail outright, while Kowtow still resolves in that line; Protect is the only line that blanks me and it merely delays into a turn where I have the speed advantage.

decisions.rationale: I'm 1v2 with Basculegion as my last Pokémon at 76%. Sucker Punch (70.8–101.5%) and Kowtow Cleave (86.2–123.1%) both KO me if I use any non-priority damaging move — after Wave Crash/LO recoil I'd be at ~37-49%, well within Sucker Punch KO range. Aqua Jet (priority +1, Speed 238 > Kingambit 70-102) would move first and make Sucker Punch fail, but Garchomp's Dragon Claw (46-67%) still hits me for a coin-flip survival, and without Tailwind next turn Garchomp outspeeds and KOs me anyway. Protect is optimal: it denies Sucker Punch (status move), wastes Garchomp's attack, preserves 76% HP, and keeps the Aqua Jet counter-Sucker-Punch play concealed for next turn when I can use it to take only Garchomp's hit. No path to winning this game exists, but Protect maximizes survival turns and keeps the most options open.

Key takeaways for games 2-3: (1) Avoid the 1v2 hole — lead differently, don't let Whimsicott die turn 1 without getting value. (2) Opponent's Garchomp has Life Orb (recoil chip each attack) and Stomping Tantrum (no EQ). (3) Opponent's Kingambit has Chople Berry + Low Kick, NO Protect — exploit with Encore/pressure. (4) Last Respects at 200 BP with 3 fainted allies is a strong nuke — the damage tool underreports it since it can't track fainted allies. (5) Opponent Charizard has SolarBeam (hits Basculegion/Garchomp SE in sun) — be wary. (6) My item edges: Basculegion Life Orb > their Mystic Water, Garchomp Roseli Berry > their Life Orb. (7) Plan: win speed control with Prankster Tailwind, use LO Basculegion as primary wallbreaker under Tailwind, leverage Aqua Jet priority to move before Kingambit's Sucker Punch.

reflections.summary: Won by dismantling their lead before Tailwind could matter. Turn 1 I Mega'd Charizard and doubled the Focus-Sash Whimsicott (Garchomp Rock Slide chip + sun-boosted Heat Wave), removing their speed-control piece immediately while their own Mega Charizard wasted the turn on Protect. Turn 2 Zard Protect blanked both their Garchomp's Rock Slide and their Zard's Ancient Power (my only real losing angle) while Garchomp's Rock Slide OHKO'd their Mega Charizard. Turn 3 I pivoted the fragile Zard out to Kingambit into Basculegion — the correct hard wall — and my Garchomp won the Chomp speed tie to KO theirs. From there Kingambit simply out-traded Basculegion (Protect stall turn 4, Sucker Punch KO turn 5). Preview plan was sound: Charizard/Garchomp/Whimsicott/Kingambit is the right four vs this mirror, and Charizard-Y was the correct Mega (Drought turns Heat Wave into an outright Whimsicott OHKO and never gives their Fairies Fairy Aura). Piloting was clean (0 errors); note two of their Rock Slides missed and I won an unrepeatable speed tie, so the margin was flattered by luck, and Whimsicott never had to move.
reflections.adjustment: Stop letting the Garchomp mirror hinge on a raw speed tie. Next game, get speed control up on my side first: either lead Whimsicott for Prankster Tailwind (so my Chomp and Kingambit move first regardless of the tie) or, when their Chomp is in front of mine, Protect/pivot Garchomp and answer with Kingambit Low Kick / Zard Solar Beam instead of Dragon Claw into the coinflip. Also plan the Basculegion swap one turn earlier — the moment their Zard or Whimsicott is gone, Kingambit should already be on the field, and use Whimsicott Encore to lock Basculegion's Protect or their Tailwind rather than leaving it as an unused back slot.
reflections.notebook:
SERIES vs mirror team (identical six species). Opponent diffs from me: their Zard has AncientPower (Rock) not SolarBeam; their Garchomp has Earthquake+PoisonJab+Roseli Berry; their Kingambit has Protect+Occa Berry and no Low Kick; their Basculegion has Life Orb. My Kingambit's Chople is dead weight; Low Kick is my mirror-breaker vs their Kingambit.
SPEED: my Zard 135, Garchomp 169, Whimsicott 184, Kingambit 81. Their Jolly Chomp 134-169 (raw tie risk - I won one tie in G1, do NOT build plans on it), Basculegion 98-130 (196-260 under Tailwind). Under their Tailwind their whole team outspeeds mine; verify same-species order with foe slot first in compare_action_order.
DAMAGE FACTS (sun): my LO Garchomp Rock Slide spread OHKOs their Mega Zard (confirmed in G1) but only 8-14% vs Roseli Chomp; Dragon Claw 69-81% into their Chomp, 40-76% into Basculegion; Rock Slide only 19-36% into Basculegion; Kingambit Kowtow Cleave 74-141% and Sucker Punch 61-117% into Basculegion (Dark 2x vs Ghost); my Zard SolarBeam 49-58% into Chomp, 65-121% into Basculegion; sun Heat Wave OHKOs their Sash Whimsicott after any chip (Rock Slide chip suffices). Their LO Adaptability Basculegion: Wave Crash 83-122% on my Mega Zard, ~42% on my Kingambit per hit (33% recoil + LO wears it down fast); their Garchomp Rock Slide 64-91% on my Mega Zard; their Mega Zard AncientPower 78-107% on my Zard - never leave Zard exposed to it.
TOOL CAUTION: estimate_damage reports Last Respects at base BP 50 and does NOT scale by fainted allies - real power is 50x(1+fainted); treat as OHKO threat on Garchomp/chipped Kingambit late.
OPPONENT TENDENCIES: brings Zard/Whimsicott/Garchomp/Basculegion (Floette and Kingambit left in back both preview slots so far). Leads with Whimsicott + a Mega Zard or Garchomp and goes for turn-1 Prankster Tailwind; will Mega and Protect with Zard on turn 1 rather than attack. Uses Basculegion Protect on the turn it expects a double (G1 turn 4). Sends Basculegion in as the revenge/cleanup piece after a KO.
PLANS: default Mega Charizard-Y (Drought re-triggers on re-entry); never Mega Floette (Fairy Aura boosts their Fairies). Turn-1 template that worked: Mega Zard + Garchomp lead, double the Sash Whimsicott (Rock Slide + Heat Wave) to blank their Tailwind turn; Zard Protect again turn 2 vs Rock Slide/AncientPower; then pivot Zard to Kingambit the instant Basculegion appears. Kingambit answers Basculegion (Last Respects 0.5x, Kowtow/Sucker 2x back); prefer Sucker Punch when it alone/with a fast partner can finish, Kowtow vs Aqua Jet/Protect reads.
FUTURE GAMES: my Whimsicott is still unused - deploy it for my own Tailwind to break the Garchomp speed tie, or Encore to lock their Protect/Tailwind. Expect them to adapt by leading Garchomp+Basculegion or finally bringing Kingambit/Floette; Low Kick answers their Occa Kingambit.

reflections.summary: Lost because Whimsicott died turn 1 after only setting Tailwind—Rock Slide chip from the opponent's Garchomp broke Focus Sash range, then Heat Wave KO'd it. Your Charizard fell turn 2 in the weather mirror, leaving you in a 1v3 hole with only Basculegion by turn 3. Once Tailwind expired, Kingambit's Sucker Punch out-prioritized Basculegion for the clean KO. The lead matchup was the root cause: Charizard+Whimsicott into Charizard+Garchomp let the opponent double-target Whimsicott for an easy turn-1 pickoff.
reflections.adjustment: Do not lead Whimsicott into their Charizard+Garchomp—it gets double-targeted and dies before providing value. Lead Garchomp+Charizard to contest the weather war and threaten their Garchomp with Dragon Claw, keeping Whimsicott or Basculegion in the back for safer Tailwind setup. If you do bring Whimsicott, pair it with Garchomp lead so Protect on Whimsicott + Garchomp attacking is an option, rather than Whimsicott being the obvious KO target next to a Protecting Charizard.
